correctness.rationale: Elliptic surgeries on hyperbolic g=6 knots give L-space fibered knots. Published bound r≤4g−1=23 and finite surgery denominator at most 2 reduce r>21 to r∈{43/2,22,45/2,23}; Ni–Zhang Table 4 places both half-integer values in genus-seven knot-Floer classes, so only r=22 or 23 remain. For Alexander polynomials, the L-space leading pair t^6−t^5 and alternating nonzero coefficients yield sixteen support patterns; Schmalian–Sivek Proposition 2.4 eliminates five patterns with odd offset of the initial missing term, leaving eleven. Their Corollary 3.7 requires a negative real zero <−1. I independently reimplemented all candidates in SymPy over exact rationals, formed Q=t^6Δ(t), and counted roots <−1 with exact Sturm sign variations: of eleven allowed patterns exactly the support {6,5,3,2,1} has one such root, yielding the displayed degree-12 symmetric polynomial. In addition, the source Remark 1.7 implies the SAME polynomial directly via irreducibility of the degree-ten factor, independently validating correctness (but destroying the originality claim). Source script checks finite support/Sturm only; no inference of existence or knot isotopy.
residual_risks: The result is a necessary implication only, not uniqueness of the knot or existence of every surgery.
The half-integer exclusions require the exact source table (not mere integrality).
The decisive polynomial implication is already in primary older work; a computational checker cannot recover novelty.

originality.rationale: DECISIVE COVERAGE: Schmalian–Sivek, arXiv:2609.39260v1, Remark 1.7 explicitly states any genus-six knot with a finite surgery of slope 22 or 23 has the SAME monodromy dilatation as P(−2,3,9). Example 3.8 explicitly gives Δ_P(t) and its negative real root −λ. Multiplying by t^6, the cited polynomial factors Q_P(t)=(t²−t+1) f(t), f(t)=t^10−t^8+t^5−t²+1. Exact finite-field factorization certifies f irreducible over Q: modulo 2, factor degrees 2 and 8; modulo 3, factor degrees 5 and 5, all factors square-free/irreducible, leaving no common proper possible rational factor degree. Thus f is the minimal polynomial of −λ. For ANY genus-six elliptic surgery at r>21, the already-published slope facts force r∈{22,23}; Remark 1.7 forces the identical λ, so its monic reciprocal Q_K=t^6Δ_K, of degree 12, is divisible by f. The residual factor is monic reciprocal quadratic t²+c t+1, and Δ_K(1)=1=f(1)·(2+c) forces c=−1. Therefore Q_K=(t²−t+1) f=Q_P. This is precisely the original entire Alexander-polynomial claim, as a short algebraic consequence of the PUBLISHED STRONGER SAME-DILATATION RESULT. It is not novel merely because the source did not display the genus-six coefficient equality separately. The existing finite Sturm enumeration is an alternative verification of a covered conclusion.
residual_risks: None that could rescue this original exact claim: the published same-dilatation statement plus normalization decisively covers it.
Possible subtleties about positive surgery half-integers do not affect the prior implication once standard Ni–Zhang table excludes them.
